text:
Maria Chen: quick intake — customer 'Pinball Analytics' surfaced a recurring issue during tenant rollouts: when traffic spikes, smart-routing falls back to a smaller quantized model mid-conversation and users see context loss / weird answers. We need a PRD to pin down scope and acceptance criteria. Problem statement, goals, non-goals, and success metrics please. :thinking:

Devon Patel: linking the incident thread + logs: https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-412 :eyes:
Devon Patel: rough TL;DR: fallback triggered when queue depth > 4k requests; fallback policy replaced model variant which dropped KV cache compatibility -> many sessions lost context.

Kevin O'Leary: a few clarifying q's before we write the PRD:
- Is customer asking for routing changes (avoid fallback) or for graceful compatibility (KV-preserving variants)?
- Are we ok making temporary slower paths (no fallback) under burst for certain tenants?

Maria Chen: Pinball asked for "no mid-conversation model swap" as a hard requirement for paid tenants. They prefer graceful degradation over silent swaps. Non-goal: full overhaul of routing engine. They'd accept either: (a) block fallback for pinned sessions and queue, or (b) ensure fallback variant is KV-compatible with main model.

Sara Gomez: acceptance criteria suggestion (first pass):
```
- No model-variant switch within a single session for >99.5% of paid-tenant sessions during peak bursts
- If fallback happens, KVs are preserved or a clear user-visible degradation message is produced
- P95 tail latency should not exceed 250ms for pinned sessions (measured over a 24h rolling window)
- No regression in quality evals: top-1 BLEU/ROUGE drop <= 1.5 points vs baseline
- Monitoring: alert when session-swap rate > 0.2% in a 1h window
```

Devon Patel: implementation options: 1) session pin + enqueue for pinned tenants (simpler platform-side policy) 2) ensure fallback model is architectural-compatible (requires model onboarding + evals) 3) hybrid: allow swap only between verified compatible variants. Each has tradeoffs on latency and unit cost.

Kevin O'Leary: edge cases to capture in PRD:
- long-running chat where tokens exceed KV cache expectations -> what to do when we exceed cache?
- multi-tenant inference on shared pods where resource pressure comes from other customers
- retries by client SDK causing duplicate sessions/mis-attribution of state
- downstream tools (plugins/functions) that expect deterministic model interface

Maria Chen: non-goals to call out: we will NOT change load balancer provider or rewrite runtime for this PRD. Also non-goal: retrofitting older quantized model formats prior to 2024.

Sara Gomez: success-metrics (proposal):
- Primary: session-swap rate during production peaks < 0.5% (monthly avg)
- Safety: alerting threshold 0.2% over 1h -> pager for eng-oncall
- Latency: p95 <= 250ms for pinned sessions; p99 soft target <= 600ms
- Cost impact: unit GPU-seconds increase <= 12% for customer tier
- Quality: automated eval delta <= 1.5 points on our prompt-suite

Devon Patel: can we add a small canary plan? Suggest: 1% of paid tenants get the new pin behavior for 48h with telemetry flags. If session-swap rate drops and latency within bounds -> roll to 25% -> 100%.

Kevin O'Leary: acceptance test matrix idea (to include in PRD): list of synthetic replay scenarios + production shadow run for 72h. Need exact test names and pass/fail thresholds.

Maria Chen: next steps: I'll draft the PRD including problem statement, goals, non-goals, acceptance criteria (Sara's list + Kevin's edge cases), rollout plan (Devon's canary suggestion), and test matrix. Can everyone review initial PRD by EOD Friday? :calendar:

product-bot: New PRD draft created: /docs/prd/no-mid-conversation-swap-2026-03-21.md (edit access: product, eng, eng-runtime)

Devon Patel: ack, will add incident repro steps and logs to the PRD.

Kevin O'Leary: ack, I'll sketch the test harness and CI steps for the shadow run.

Sara Gomez: ack — will enumerate monitoring dashboard panels + alert runbooks.

Maria Chen: thanks — I'll ping again once draft is up. :thumbsup:
